01.event: People asked Rabbi Elai where Rabbi Abbahu was hiding.
01.turn: Rabbi Elai answered in a riddle: Abbahu had consulted the Nasi and gone south to the Sages there.
01.summary: Rabbi Abbahu had disappeared, and people asked Rabbi Elai to show them where he was hiding. Rabbi Elai answered cryptically that Abbahu had taken counsel with 'the one who crowns' (the Nasi) and had gone south to 'Mephibosheth', meaning the Sages of the south.
01.missing: Why Abbahu was hiding and what came of it are not told; the exchange is only a clever reply.

03.event: Rav arrived at Apsetaya and forbade climbing even a stripped tree on Shabbat.
03.turn: The Gemara explains he did it not because it was prohibited but because the place was lax and needed a fence.
03.summary: Rav came to a place called Apsetaya and forbade its residents to climb even a tree already stripped of its branches on Shabbat. The Gemara explains that this was not the strict law: Rav found a place where transgression was common and added a safeguard.
03.missing: Only a bare report of a ruling; no reaction or consequence is told.

04.actor: Ameimar, a woman seeking a tenth of her father's estate, and her brothers
04.event: A woman came before Ameimar demanding a tenth of her father's estate as her dowry share.
04.turn: Her brothers said they would pay her off in cash if they had the money, and Ameimar, who had held a daughter is an heir, said nothing against it.
04.outcome: Rav Minyumi, who witnessed it, concluded Ameimar had retracted and now treated her as a creditor.
04.summary: Rav Minyumi was standing before Ameimar when a woman came asking for a tenth of her father's estate. Her brothers told her that if they had the money they would pay her off in cash, and Ameimar stayed silent. From his silence Rav Minyumi understood that Ameimar had abandoned his view that a daughter inherits, and now treated her as a creditor who can be paid in money.

05.event: A sharecropper betrothed a woman with a handful of onions taken from the field he worked.
05.turn: Rava asked him who had given him the onions, meaning they were stolen.
05.summary: A sharecropper betrothed a woman using a handful of onions from the field he worked and then asked Rava whether she was betrothed. Rava asked him who had given him permission to take them: they were stolen, so the betrothal failed. The Gemara adds that had he taken a whole bundle, he could have claimed it as his share of the crop.

08.actor: A fox and the people who weighed a turnip
08.event: A fox made its nest inside a turnip.
08.turn: When the turnip was weighed, it still came to sixty litra by the Tzippori measure.
08.summary: To show that future wheat kernels as large as an ox's kidneys are not unbelievable, the Sages cite an incident: a fox nested inside a turnip, and when people weighed the hollowed turnip it still weighed sixty litra by the measure of Tzippori.
08.missing: It is a cited marvel rather than a full story; no one's situation changes.

09.event: Ravina, holding wine belonging to his orphaned nephew, was taking his own wine to Sikhra to sell.
09.turn: He asked Rav Ashi whether he could take the orphan's wine along with his own.
09.outcome: Rav Ashi told him to go, since the orphan's wine is no better than his own.
09.summary: Ravina was looking after wine belonging to his orphaned nephew, Ravina the younger, and was taking his own wine to Sikhra to sell. He asked Rav Ashi whether he could take the orphan's wine with him. Rav Ashi told him to go ahead: if this was good enough for his own wine, it was good enough for the orphan's.

10.actor: A man who conditioned a bill of divorce
10.event: A man told witnesses that if he did not marry his betrothed by the New Moon of Adar, the document would be a bill of divorce.
10.turn: When Adar came, he claimed he had said Nisan.
10.summary: A man told witnesses that if he did not marry his betrothed by the New Moon of Adar, a bill of divorce would take effect. When the date arrived he claimed he had actually said Nisan. The Gemara then weighs the legal concerns without saying how the case was decided.
10.missing: The ruling or outcome of the case is not stated.

12.actor: The Sages examining a found bill of divorce
12.event: A bill of divorce was found in Sura in the name of Anan bar Hiyya of Neharde'a.
12.turn: The Sages found only one other man of that name, and witnesses said he was in Neharde'a the day it was written.
12.summary: A bill of divorce was found in Sura, written by 'Anan bar Hiyya of Neharde'a'. The Sages searched all the way from Sura to Neharde'a and found only one other man with that name, Anan bar Hiyya of Hagra, and witnesses testified he had been with them in Neharde'a that day. Abaye and Rava then argue over whether to worry about him, but no decision about the woman is told.
12.missing: What was done with the bill of divorce is not stated; the rest is legal argument.

13.actor: Rabbi Abba bar Shumni and Rav Menashya bar Yirmeya
13.event: Two scholars parting at the ford of the Yofti River agreed each would say a teaching the other had not heard.
13.outcome: Each one offered a teaching: one defined tipsy vs drunk, the other how to keep a convert's property.
13.summary: Rabbi Abba bar Shumni and Rav Menashya bar Yirmeya were taking leave of each other at the ford of the Yofti River. Following the advice to part with a word of halakha, they agreed each would say something new to the other. One explained the difference between someone who has drunk and someone who is drunk; the other taught that one who takes a convert's property should buy a Torah scroll with it.
13.missing: The frame is a narrative but nothing turns; it serves to deliver teachings.

14.event: Rav Hisda's daughter asked her father, who studied through the nights, whether he wanted to sleep a little.
14.turn: He replied that long days of no opportunity are coming, and then he will sleep plenty.
14.outcome: He kept studying, implying he would rest only in death.
14.summary: Rav Hisda used to spend his nights studying. His daughter asked him whether he did not want to sleep a little. He answered that long days, short in chances to study and do mitzvot, would soon come, and then he would sleep a great deal, meaning after his death.

15.event: A dying Madonite wanted to give away much movable property as a gift.
15.turn: The Sages told him it could only be done through land, so he bought a small rocky plot and gave the goods along with portions of it.
15.outcome: He died, and the Sages carried out his instructions.
15.summary: A Madonite in Jerusalem, ill and short of time, had many movable goods he wanted to give away. The Sages told him the only way was to transfer them together with land. He bought a plot near Jerusalem and declared that its northern part, along with a hundred sheep and a hundred barrels, went to a certain person. He died, and the Sages honoured what he had said.

16.actor: The returning exiles and their prophets
16.event: The exiles returning from Babylonia camped at the Heker well.
16.turn: The prophets among them permitted them to draw from it on a Festival, following an ancestral custom.
16.summary: When the exiles came back from Babylonia they camped by a particular Heker well, and the prophets among them allowed them to draw water from it on a Festival. The text clarifies that the prophets were really confirming a custom passed down from their forefathers.
16.missing: Little more than a report of a permission; no development or consequence.

17.actor: The people of Neharde'a and Rav Nahman
17.event: During a drought in Neharde'a everyone sold their mansions to buy wheat.
17.turn: Then wheat arrived and the sales proved unnecessary.
17.outcome: Rav Nahman ruled that the mansions go back to their owners.
17.summary: A drought struck Neharde'a and everyone sold their mansions to buy food. Soon afterwards a shipment of wheat arrived, making the sales pointless. Rav Nahman ruled that the mansions must be returned to their original owners.

18.actor: Mar Yehuda, Rav Yosef, Rav Shmuel son of Rabba bar bar Hana, and Rabba
18.event: Mar Yehuda found two scholars at the door of Rabba's study hall and challenged them with a contradiction about Rabbi Shimon's view.
18.turn: They were silent and had no answer, so they went to Rabba.
18.outcome: Rabba said a quarrelsome person had put them up to it and resolved the contradiction.
18.summary: Mar Yehuda came upon Rav Yosef and Rav Shmuel standing at the entrance of Rabba's study hall and posed them a contradiction between two teachings of Rabbi Shimon about animals slaughtered in the Temple courtyard. They had no answer and fell silent. They took the question to Rabba, who remarked that a quarrelsome man had set them up, and then explained that the first teaching dealt with an animal found to be a tereifa.

19.event: Rabbi Zeira was avoiding his teacher Rav Yehuda because he wanted to move to Eretz Yisrael.
19.turn: Rav Yehuda held that leaving Babylonia for the Land violates a commandment.
19.summary: Rabbi Zeira wanted to go up to the Land of Israel, so he kept out of sight of his teacher Rav Yehuda, who taught that anyone leaving Babylonia for Israel transgresses a positive commandment.
19.missing: Whether Rabbi Zeira went and what happened next are not in the segments shown; [3] gives only the verse and Rabbi Zeira's reading of it.

20.actor: A man who sold his mother's marriage contract, Rami bar Hama and Rava
20.event: A man sold his expected rights to his mother's marriage contract, saying he would not refund if his mother objected.
20.turn: His mother died without objecting, and he himself then contested the sale.
20.outcome: Rava ruled against him: he had guaranteed the sale against his own objections even if not his mother's.
20.summary: A man sold, for a small sum, his future right to collect his mother's marriage contract, telling the buyer he would not refund the money if his mother objected. His mother died without objecting, and then he himself challenged the sale. Rami bar Hama thought he stood in his mother's place, but Rava ruled that he had certainly guaranteed the sale against his own objections, so the sale stood.
